title: OpenVA Hosted Job Record
description: Operational metadata for one hosted resolver VERIFY-mode job in the durable job store. (Cached mode is synchronous and creates no job record.) Data-minimised and transient by design: it carries NO uploaded inventory content, NO vendor identity strings, and NO request bodies. The submitted request lives separately in a transient request envelope (referenced by request_ref) and the result in a transient result blob (referenced by result_ref); both are TTL-deleted. Expiry is time-based on expires_at (the API returns 410 once now >= expires_at); there is no persisted 'expired' state. There is NO deduplication in v1: every request creates a new job, and there is no content-derived dedup key (any future idempotency option must use a server-keyed HMAC bound to an authenticated caller, never a dictionary-testable content digest). Result access requires the separate job_token capability (stored only as job_token_digest); job_id is a loggable correlation id, not a credential. additionalProperties is false and state-dependent invariants are enforced below so a leaked or inconsistent field fails validation. Operational metadata only; not legal, compliance, procurement, security, KYC, AML, audit, or vendor-risk advice.

job_id.description: Opaque correlation id (an opaque UUID). Carries no submitted content and is NOT an access credential; safe to log. Result access requires the separate job_token capability (stored here only as job_token_digest).

job_token_digest.description: SHA-256 of the high-entropy job_token capability returned once at creation. The token gates result polling/retrieval; it is never logged and never stored in plaintext — only this digest persists for verification.

freshness_mode.description: Job records exist only for verify-mode async work; cached mode is synchronous and creates no record.

request_ref.description: Opaque pointer to the TRANSIENT request envelope (submitted input) the worker reads. Non-null while the job is non-terminal; null once the envelope is deleted on the terminal transition. Never the input itself.

row_count.description: A verify job's row count, bounded by the authoritative hosted_verify_limits.max_verify_rows (NOT the larger cached/batch limits.max_rows_cached). Over-limit requests are rejected by the API before a job exists.

result_ref.description: Opaque pointer to the transient result blob (TTL-deleted). Non-null only when completed.

error_code.description: Stable, generic JOB failure code (never an upstream message or submitted content). Non-null only when failed. input_too_large / row_limit_exceeded are API pre-job rejection responses, NOT job failures, so they are not in this vocabulary.

attempt.description: Bounded EXECUTION retry counter, owned by the watchdog. REQUIRED (not merely defaulted): the watchdog compares and increments it to terminalize a job once the retry bound is reached, so a missing counter would break bounded recovery. A newly received record is 0 (enforced below) and stays 0 until execution; each watchdog recovery (executing -> queued/failed) increments it; reaching the maximum terminalizes the job to failed. This is NOT the dispatch recovery counter — see dispatch_attempt.

dispatch_attempt.description: Bounded DISPATCH (enqueue) recovery generation, owned by the reconciler — distinct from attempt (execution retries, watchdog). 0 is the original API enqueue (Cloud Task name = job_id, no suffix). While a job remains received, the reconciler atomically increments this (CAS) BEFORE re-enqueueing and names the new Cloud Task {job_id}-r{dispatch_attempt}, so every recovery uses a fresh, never-tombstoned name (the first recovery is r1, never the tombstoned r0). It can advance while received (so it is NOT pinned to 0 like attempt); beyond the maximum the reconciler stops re-enqueueing and the job terminates by time-based expiry (410 -> 404).

lease_owner.description: Execution lease holder (the worker instance id). Non-null only while executing; a stale lease (lease_expires_at < now) is recovered by the watchdog. Carries no submitted content.

lease_expires_at.description: When the execution lease goes stale; the worker heartbeats to extend it. Non-null only while executing.

allOf.$comment: received: a newly accepted job has not been retried yet, so attempt is 0.
received/queued: live envelope, no result/error, and NOT yet leased.
executing: live envelope, no result/error, and a live execution lease.
completed has a result, no error, the envelope is deleted, and the lease is released.
failed has a generic error, no result, the envelope is deleted, and the lease is released.
